metadata.title: Layer Normalization (Ba, Kiros, Hinton, 2016)
metadata.framework: normalization of layer inputs across the feature dimension within each example, independent of batch
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1607.06450.

nodes.name: Limitation of batch normalization for RNNs
nodes.statement: Batch normalization is not directly applicable to recurrent neural networks because: (1) it requires storing separate statistics for each time step, (2) variable-length sequences make this impractical, and (3) at test time, mini-batch statistics are unavailable for single-example inference in sequence models.

nodes.name: Layer normalization transform
nodes.statement: For a single training example with hidden vector $\mathbf{h} \in \mathbb{R}^H$, the layer normalization transform computes statistics over all $H$ hidden units within that example: $\mu = \frac{1}{H} \sum_{i=1}^{H} h_i$, $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{H} \sum_{i=1}^{H} (h_i - \mu)^2$, $\hat{h}_i = \frac{h_i - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \epsilon}}$, $y_i = \gamma_i \hat{h}_i + \beta_i$, where $\gamma, \beta \in \mathbb{R}^H$ are learnable gain and bias parameters. Unlike BN, the normalization is over features within one example, not over examples within a batch.

nodes.name: Layer normalization in RNNs
nodes.statement: In an RNN with hidden state $\mathbf{h}^t = f(W_h \mathbf{h}^{t-1} + W_x \mathbf{x}^t + \mathbf{b})$, layer normalization is applied to the pre-activation summed input: $\mathbf{a}^t = W_h \mathbf{h}^{t-1} + W_x \mathbf{x}^t$, then $\mathbf{h}^t = f(\mathrm{LN}(\mathbf{a}^t))$ where $\mathrm{LN}$ normalizes across the $H$ dimensions of $\mathbf{a}^t$. The same $\gamma, \beta$ are shared across time steps.

nodes.name: Invariance properties of layer normalization
nodes.statement: Layer normalization has the following invariance properties: (1) It is invariant to re-scaling of individual weights: scaling a row of the weight matrix does not change the normalized output. (2) It is invariant to re-centering of individual weights. (3) It is NOT invariant to re-scaling of the dataset, unlike batch normalization. These properties complement those of BN.

nodes.name: Comparison of normalization axes
nodes.statement: BN normalizes over the batch dimension for each feature: $\mu_k^{\mathrm{BN}} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m h_k^{(i)}$. LN normalizes over the feature dimension for each example: $\mu^{\mathrm{LN},(i)} = \frac{1}{H} \sum_{k=1}^H h_k^{(i)}$. Both use learnable affine parameters $\gamma, \beta$ after normalization.

nodes.name: Geometry of LN gradient (Fisher information interpretation)
nodes.statement: Under a GLM interpretation where the pre-activation is $a_i^l = w_i^{l \top} h^{l-1}$, the Fisher information matrix for the weights has a block structure. Layer normalization implicitly performs a form of natural gradient descent by normalizing the pre-activations, analogous to how BN relates to the Fisher information of the batch statistics.
assumptions: Generalized linear model interpretation of a single layer
conclusions: LN gradient update has an implicit Fisher-information scaling
LN stabilizes the geometry of the loss surface

nodes.name: LN on order embeddings and skip-thought vectors
nodes.statement: Layer normalization applied to LSTM-based skip-thought encoders and order-embedding models yields faster convergence and improved generalization compared to baseline (no normalization) and in some cases compared to batch normalization.

nodes.name: LN on image-caption and question-answering
nodes.statement: On attentive reader models for question answering and image-caption retrieval, LN provides consistent speedups in training (reaching baseline performance in fewer updates) and modest improvements in final performance.

nodes.name: LN on convolutional networks (limited benefit)
nodes.statement: On convolutional networks (CIFAR-10 and ImageNet), layer normalization does not improve over batch normalization. The authors conjecture this is because in CNNs the features within a channel have different roles (edge detectors vs. textures), making cross-feature normalization less appropriate than cross-batch normalization.
